verses.1:1: Paul and Timothy, bondservants of Christ Jesus, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, together with the overseers and deacons:
verses.1:2: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:3: I give thanks to my God upon every remembrance of you,
verses.1:4: always in every supplication of mine for you all, making my supplication with joy,
verses.1:5: on account of your fellowship in the gospel from the first day even until now,
verses.1:6: being persuaded of this very thing, that He who began a good work in you will bring it to perfection until the day of Christ Jesus;
verses.1:7: even as it is right for me to be thus minded concerning all of you, because I hold you in my heart, seeing that both in my chains and in the defense and confirmation of the gospel, you are all fellow partakers with me of grace.
verses.1:8: For God is my witness how earnestly I long for all of you with the tender affection of Christ Jesus.
verses.1:9: And this is my prayer, that your love may abound yet more and more in full knowledge and all discernment,
verses.1:10: so that you may test and approve the things that are excellent, and so be pure and without offense until the day of Christ,
verses.1:11: being filled with the fruit of righteousness which is through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
verses.1:12: Now I desire you to know, brethren, that the things concerning me have rather served for the advancement of the gospel,
verses.1:13: so that my chains have become evident in Christ throughout the entire praetorian guard and to all the rest,
verses.1:14: and most of the brethren in the Lord, having gained confidence through my chains, are far more bold to speak the word of God without fear.
verses.1:15: Some indeed preach Christ even out of envy and strife, and others also out of goodwill;
verses.1:16: the latter preach out of love, knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the gospel;
verses.1:17: while the former proclaim Christ out of selfish ambition, not sincerely, supposing to stir up affliction in my chains.
verses.1:18: What then? Only that in every manner, whether in pretense or in truth, Christ is proclaimed; and in this I rejoice. Yes, and I shall rejoice,
verses.1:19: for I know that through your supplication and the provision of the Spirit of Jesus Christ this will turn out for my deliverance,
verses.1:20: according to my eager expectation and hope that I shall not be put to shame in anything, but that with all boldness, as always, so now as well Christ shall be magnified in my body, whether by life or by death.
verses.1:21: For to me, to live means Christ, and to die means gain.
verses.1:22: Yet if I am to go on living in the flesh, this will mean fruit of labor for me—and which I shall choose I cannot tell.
verses.1:23: Indeed, I am hard pressed between the two, having the desire to depart and to be with Christ, for that is far better indeed;
verses.1:24: yet to remain on in the flesh is more necessary on your account.
verses.1:25: And being persuaded of this, I know that I shall abide and continue with you all for your advancement and joy of the faith,
verses.1:26: so that in me your ground for glorying in Christ Jesus may abound through my coming to you again.
verses.1:27: Only conduct yourselves as citizens worthy of the gospel of Christ, so that whether I come and see you or remain absent, I may hear concerning you that you stand firm in one spirit, with one soul contending together for the faith of the gospel,
verses.1:28: and not frightened in anything by those who oppose you, which to them is a clear sign of destruction, yet of your salvation, and that from God;
verses.1:29: for to you it has been graciously granted on behalf of Christ, not only to believe in Him, but also to suffer for His sake,
verses.1:30: engaged in the same conflict that you saw in me and now hear to be in me.
verses.2:1: Therefore, if there is any encouragement in Christ, if any consolation of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any tender affection and compassion,
verses.2:2: make my joy full by being of the same mind, keeping the same love, being of one soul, and of one purpose,
verses.2:3: doing nothing out of selfish ambition or vainglory, but in humility of mind esteeming one another above yourselves,
verses.2:4: each of you looking not only to his own concerns, but each also to the concerns of others.
verses.2:5: Keep this mind among yourselves, which was also in Christ Jesus,
verses.2:6: who, existing in the form of God, did not reckon being equal with God a prize to be grasped,
verses.2:7: but emptied Himself, taking the form of a bondservant and coming to be in the likeness of men; and being found in appearance as a man,
verses.2:8: He humbled Himself, becoming obedient even to death—even the death of a cross.
verses.2:9: Therefore God also exalted Him exceedingly, and graciously bestowed upon Him the name which is above every name,
verses.2:10: so that at the name of Jesus every knee may bow, of those in heaven, of those upon the earth, and of those beneath the earth,
verses.2:11: and every tongue may openly confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
verses.2:12: So then, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed—not only as in my presence, but now far more in my absence—work out your own salvation with fear and trembling,
verses.2:13: for God is the One working in you both to will and to act for the sake of His good pleasure.
verses.2:14: Do everything without murmurings and disputes,
verses.2:15: so that you may prove to be blameless and pure, children of God without blemish in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation, among whom you shine as luminaries in the world,
verses.2:16: holding fast the word of life, so that I may have cause to glory on the day of Christ, that I did not run in vain nor labor in vain.
verses.2:17: Yet even if I am poured out as a drink offering upon the sacrifice and sacred service of your faith, I rejoice and share my joy with all of you;
verses.2:18: and in the same manner you also rejoice, and share your joy with me.
verses.2:19: Now I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I also may be of good cheer upon learning how it goes with you.
verses.2:20: For I have no one of like spirit who will genuinely care for your concerns,
verses.2:21: for all seek their own concerns, not the things of Jesus Christ.
verses.2:22: Yet you know his proven character, that as a child with a father he served alongside me for the gospel.
verses.2:23: Him, therefore, I hope to send immediately, as soon as I see how matters stand with me;
verses.2:24: and I am confident in the Lord that I myself shall also come soon.
verses.2:25: Yet I have deemed it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier, and your messenger and minister to my need,
verses.2:26: because he was yearning for all of you and was sorely distressed because you heard that he was ill.
verses.2:27: For indeed he was ill, nearly to the point of death; yet God had mercy on him, and not on him alone, but also on me, lest I should have sorrow upon sorrow.
verses.2:28: Therefore I have sent him the more eagerly, so that seeing him again you may rejoice, and I may be freer from sorrow.
verses.2:29: Welcome him, therefore, in the Lord with all joy, and hold such men in honor,
verses.2:30: because for the work of Christ he came close to death, hazarding his life in order to complete what was lacking in your service toward me.
verses.3:1: Finally, my brethren, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you is not wearisome to me, and for you it is a safeguard.
verses.3:2: Beware of the dogs, beware of the wicked workers, beware of the mutilation.
verses.3:3: For we are the circumcision, who worship by the Spirit of God, and glory in Christ Jesus, and place no confidence in the flesh,
verses.3:4: though I myself also have reason for confidence in the flesh. If anyone else thinks he may trust in the flesh, I even more:
verses.3:5: circumcised on the eighth day, of the lineage of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; as to the law, a Pharisee;
verses.3:6: as to zeal, persecuting the church; as to the righteousness that is in the law, proved blameless.
verses.3:7: Yet whatever things were gains to me, these I have reckoned as loss for the sake of Christ.
verses.3:8: More than that, I also reckon all things to be loss on account of the surpassing worth of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, for whose sake I have suffered the loss of all things, and I consider them as refuse, so that I may gain Christ
verses.3:9: and be found in Him, not having a righteousness of my own that comes from the law, but that which is through faith in Christ, the righteousness from God resting upon faith,
verses.3:10: that I may know Him, and the power of His resurrection, and fellowship in His sufferings, becoming conformed to His death,
verses.3:11: if by any means I may reach the resurrection from among the dead.
verses.3:12: Not that I have already obtained it, or have already been made perfect; rather, I press forward, if indeed I may take hold of that for which I was also taken hold of by Christ Jesus.
verses.3:13: Brethren, I do not consider myself to have taken hold of it; but one thing I do: forgetting the things that lie behind and straining forward to the things that lie ahead,
verses.3:14: I press onward toward the goal for the prize of God's upward calling in Christ Jesus.
verses.3:15: Therefore, as many of us as are mature, let us be of this mind; and if in anything you think otherwise, God will reveal this also to you.
verses.3:16: Nevertheless, to the measure we have already attained, let us walk in the same way.
verses.3:17: Brethren, join in imitating me, and keep your eyes on those who walk in this way, just as you have us for a pattern.
verses.3:18: For many walk, of whom I often spoke to you, and now tell you even weeping, as the enemies of the cross of Christ:
verses.3:19: whose end is destruction, whose god is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame—those whose minds are fixed upon earthly things.
verses.3:20: For our citizenship exists in heaven, from which we also eagerly await a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.3:21: who shall transform the body of our humiliation to be conformed to the body of His glory, according to the working by which He is able even to subject all things to Himself.
verses.4:1: Therefore, my brethren, beloved and longed for, my joy and my crown, stand firm thus in the Lord, beloved.
verses.4:2: I urge Euodia, and I urge Syntyche, to be of one mind in the Lord.
verses.4:3: Yes, I ask you also, true yokefellow, assist these women, who contended alongside me in the gospel, together with Clement also and the rest of my fellow laborers, whose names are in the book of life.
verses.4:4: Rejoice in the Lord always; again I shall say, rejoice.
verses.4:5: Let your forbearance be known to all men. The Lord is near.
verses.4:6: Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything, by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let your petitions be made known to God;
verses.4:7: and the peace of God, which transcends all understanding, shall guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.
verses.4:8: Finally, brethren, whatever things are true, whatever things are honorable, whatever things are righteous, whatever things are pure, whatever things are lovely, whatever things are of good repute—if there is any virtue and if there is anything worthy of praise, ponder these things.
verses.4:9: What you have learned and received and heard and seen in me, put these things into practice; and the God of peace shall be with you.
verses.4:10: Now I rejoiced greatly in the Lord that now at length you have revived your concern for me; indeed, you were already concerned, yet you lacked opportunity.
verses.4:11: Not that I speak because of want, for I have learned, in whatever state I find myself, to be content.
verses.4:12: I know how to be brought low, and I know also how to abound. In every situation and in all things I have learned the secret both of being filled and of going hungry, both of abounding and of suffering want.
verses.4:13: I have strength for all things in Him who empowers me.
verses.4:14: Nevertheless, you have done well by sharing with me in my affliction.
verses.4:15: Now you yourselves also know, Philippians, that in the beginning of the gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no church shared with me in the account of giving and receiving except you alone;
verses.4:16: for even in Thessalonica you sent once and again to supply my need.
verses.4:17: Not that I seek the gift, rather I seek the fruit that multiplies to your account.
verses.4:18: Indeed, I have received everything in full and have an abundance; I am well supplied, having received from Epaphroditus the things sent from you, a fragrant aroma, an acceptable sacrifice, well-pleasing to God.
verses.4:19: And my God shall supply every need of yours according to His riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
verses.4:20: Now to our God and Father be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.4:21: Greet every saint in Christ Jesus. The brethren who are with me send greetings to you.
verses.4:22: All the saints send you greetings, and especially those of Caesar's household.
verses.4:23: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

notes.1:7: The Greek infinitive clause can be construed either as 'because I hold you in my heart' (the most common reading) or 'because you hold me in your heart.'
notes.1:13: The Greek term praitorion refers either to the elite imperial (praetorian) guard stationed in Rome or to the governor's official headquarters.
notes.1:16: The critical Greek text places the group preaching out of love in verse 16 and the group acting out of selfish ambition in verse 17, reversing the order found in the Majority Text.
notes.1:27: The Greek verb politeuomai literally means 'to conduct oneself as a citizen,' an apt metaphor for believers living in the Roman colony of Philippi.
notes.2:5: The Greek omits the verb in the second clause, allowing either an ethical reading ('which was also in Christ Jesus') or a relational reading ('which is also yours in Christ Jesus').
notes.2:6: The rare Greek noun harpagmos ('a prize to be grasped') can denote either something not yet possessed to be seized or an existing privilege to be exploited for self-advantage.
notes.2:16: The Greek participle epechontes can mean either 'holding fast' (clinging firmly to the gospel) or 'holding forth' (offering the word of life to the world).
notes.2:30: The critical Greek text reads paraboleusamenos ('risking' or 'hazarding' one's life), whereas later manuscripts read parabouleusamenos ('disregarding' one's life).
notes.3:3: The Greek critical text reads "by the Spirit of God" (pneumati theou), whereas later manuscripts read "worship God in spirit."
notes.3:8: The Greek term skybala denotes refuse, scraps, or dung, stressing the utter worthlessness of Paul's former credentials compared with knowing Christ.
notes.3:9: The phrase "faith in Christ" (pisteos Christou) can also be translated "the faithfulness of Christ," and interpreters debate whether Christ is the object or the subject of this faith.
notes.3:16: The Greek critical text preserves a shorter reading here without the later expansion "by the same rule, let us be of the same mind"; the verb stoichein means to keep in step or walk in line with.
notes.3:20: The Greek noun politeuma means "citizenship" or "commonwealth," a term of special resonance for believers living in the Roman colony of Philippi.
notes.4:3: The Greek phrase gnesie syzyge ("true yokefellow" or "loyal companion") may address an unnamed co-worker, though some take Syzygus as a proper name.
notes.4:12: The verb memyemai ("I have learned the secret") originally referred to initiation into a mystery, here depicting Paul's hard-won spiritual contentment.
notes.4:13: The earliest Greek manuscripts read simply "in Him who empowers me," without explicitly adding "Christ" as in later manuscripts.
notes.4:23: The Greek critical text reads "with your spirit," whereas the later Byzantine manuscript tradition reads "with you all."
